newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: More Malaysian politicians get booted out.
newsitem.headline: More Malaysian politicians get booted out.

text.p: A powerful Malaysian state politician will be kicked out of his job on Friday as a campaign against corruption gathers momentum, sources close to acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.

Mohamed Aini Taib, the second-ranking executive in the central state of Selangor, would be dropped from the state's executive committee, the sources said on Friday. The announcement was expected later in the day, senior aides to Anwar told Reuters.
It would be the latest in a series of sackings in a high-profile campaign to clean up government.

On Thursday, Deputy Primary Industries Minister Siti Zainab Abu Bakar was sacked from her post and also suspended as a member of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO).

Zainab and Senator Habshah Osman, who was also suspended as an UMNO member, were accused of diverting 1.8 million ringgit ($716,000) from the UMNO women's wing accounts. Siti was the former treasurer of UMNO Women and Habshah its former secretary. The suspensions, announced after a meeting of UMNO's Supreme Council, was chaired by Anwar in the absence of Mahathir, who is on an extended leave abroad.

In a video-conference link-up from London, Mahathir congratulated the Supreme Council on making the move, urging them "to support this and any future decisions on this matter just as the cabinet has done".

Aini, the Selangor executive, was barred from contesting a Supreme Council seat in last year's UMNO party elections after the leadership accused him of "money politics", which covers a host of sins including vote buying.
It was not immediately clear why he would be dropped from his state job.
Aini was roundly criticised last year as well for banning a Michael Jackson concert at a stadium that is in a muncipality in which he is council president.

Former Selangor chief minister Muhammad Muhammad Taib quit his state and party posts under pressure from the UNMO Supreme Council in April after he was caught in Australia's Brisbane airport in January with A$1.2 million in undeclared cash.

On Monday, a lawmaker from Malacca state was charged with abusing his position in approving state land for a commercial development, while an aide to the late chief minister of that state was accused in court of accepting a Mercedes Benz to expedite approval of an investment project.

Sahar Arpan, the lawmaker in the Malacca land case, faces a maximum 14 years imprisonment and fine of 20,000 ringgit. Azman Ghani, the political aide accused of accepting the Mercedes, is liable to two years in jail if convicted, prosecutors said. Sahar and Azman pleaded not guilty.

Financial market analysts have speculated that Mahathir had planned the crackdown to coincide with his two-month leave in Europe, with Deputy Prime Minister Anwar formally given charge of both the government and UMNO.
"He's not around...they can't run to him," said one analyst, referring to Mahathir and a popular theory that politicians in trouble often seek his help.
The blitz against high-ranking officials was also read by some analysts as Mahathir's way of testing Anwar, 49, who is hoping to succeed the 71-year-old Mahathir.

Mahathir and Anwar have frequently expressed concern that Malaysia's economic boom has created a materialistic culture and that political party positions are increasingly viewed as a quick way of getting rich.
